Container.Name: A-Eye
Container.Overview: A-Eye is a self-hosted AI photo intelligence tool. This is a fork of the original A-Eye by SpaceinvaderOne (https://github.com/SpaceinvaderOne/a-eye), created to fix bugs present in the original. Uses a local vision model (Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible server such as Halogen, llama.cpp or vLLM) to understand, describe, tag, and rename your photos — no cloud required, everything runs on your own hardware. Supports automatic renaming, manual review mode, XMP sidecar writing (compatible with Immich, Lightroom, and digiKam), natural language photo search, quality detection for blurry or accidental shots, and a temporary workspace for processing photos from other devices. Works as a full photo renamer, a metadata enrichment tool, or a non-destructive read-only catalogue. This fork adds OpenAI-compatible servers with an option to turn off model thinking for much faster tagging, and the API endpoints the Eyeris photo manager uses to send untagged photos and videos for analysis.
Container.Requires: Requires a running Ollama instance with a vision model pulled, e.g. minicpm-v. Run: docker exec ollama ollama pull minicpm-v

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port for the A-Eye web interface.

Config.Name: Photos Directory
Config.Description: Path to your photos directory. A-Eye will scan and process images from here.

Config.Name: App Data
Config.Description: Persistent storage for the database, config, and thumbnail cache.

Config.Name: Ollama Host
Config.Description: URL of the AI server: Ollama (e.g. http://192.168.1.x:11434) or an OpenAI-compatible server (e.g. http://192.168.1.x:8731). Use the server's LAN IP — not localhost (that resolves inside the container).

Config.Name: AI API
Config.Description: API type of the server above: ollama (native Ollama API) or openai (any OpenAI-compatible server such as Halogen, llama.cpp or vLLM).

Config.Name: AI API Key
Config.Description: Bearer token for OpenAI-compatible servers that require one. Leave empty for Ollama and Halogen.

Config.Name: Disable Thinking
Config.Description: Ask reasoning models (Qwen, Halogen) to answer without a thinking phase: much faster tagging.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that owns your photos directory. Run 'id -u' on your Unraid terminal to find yours. Default 99 = nobody.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that owns your photos directory. Run 'id -g' on your Unraid terminal to find yours. Default 100 = users.
